title: VizBind: a declarative RDF vocabulary for notation-independent visualization of RDFS/OWL models
description:
VizBind is a declarative RDF vocabulary that describes an ontology visual notation as data rather than as tool code. A notation is a set of binding rules, each separating selection of model constructs (via SPARQL), mapping to abstract visual constructs (node, edge, compartment, decorator), and engine-agnostic styling, with priority-based conflict resolution. The same RDFS/OWL model renders into different notations by swapping one file, and the same notation renders through different engines.

This deposit contains the binding vocabulary, two notations (a VOWL subset and a structurally contrasting UML-style notation), a proof-of-concept Python engine with Graphviz, Mermaid and Cytoscape.js adapters, six example ontologies, and the evaluation scripts that regenerate every figure and every number reported in the accompanying KEOD 2026 paper.

Research artifact for: Suchánek, M. and Pecka, J. (2026). Binding Ontologies to Notation: A Declarative RDF Vocabulary for Notation-Independent Visualisation of RDFS/OWL Models. KEOD 2026, SCITEPRESS.
